_about: Desk and sitting problems: why they happen, what you may notice, and short moves to break them up. Screens and trains only; never a diagnosis. Exercise ids come from backend/data/exercises.json, data/exercises-desk.json and data/exercises-extra.json.

problems.title: Tight hip flexors and a forward-tipped pelvis
problems.why: Hours of sitting keep the front of the hip short, and the muscles can feel stiff when you stand. That stiffness can tip the pelvis forward and push the low back into more arch.
signs: The front of the hips feels tight when you first stand up
Standing tall makes your low back feel arched or tired
You lean forward for the first few steps

problems.title: Sleepy glutes from sitting on them
problems.why: Sitting compresses the glutes and they get little work all day. When they are slow to switch on, the low back and hamstrings tend to take over in standing and walking.
signs: Your buttocks feel numb or flat after a long sit
Standing up you push off the desk or your thighs
One side feels weaker on stairs

problems.title: Forward head and neck strain
problems.why: Looking at a screen pulls the head forward of the shoulders, and the neck muscles hold it there for hours. The deep front neck muscles tire and the back of the neck and upper shoulders take the strain.
signs: Ache at the base of the skull or top of the shoulders by mid afternoon
Your chin pokes toward the screen
Headaches after long screen days

problems.title: Rounded upper back and shoulders
problems.why: Reaching for the keyboard rounds the shoulders forward and the upper back follows. The chest muscles shorten and the muscles between the shoulder blades lose endurance.
signs: Shoulders sit forward when you look side-on
Upper back feels stiff when you sit tall
Reaching overhead feels blocked

problems.title: Low-back stiffness and pressure after long sitting
problems.why: Staying in one position for a long time leaves the low back stiff, and slumped sitting loads the discs in a bent position. Changing position often matters more than finding one perfect posture.
signs: Stiff and slow for the first minutes after standing
An ache that eases once you walk around
You keep shifting in the chair

problems.title: Tight hamstrings and sciatic irritation from slumping
problems.why: Slumping with the legs out puts the nerve at the back of the leg under gentle tension for long periods. The hamstrings can feel tight when it is actually the nerve that is sensitive.
signs: Tightness behind the thigh or knee after sitting
A pull down the leg when you straighten it while slumped
Tingling that eases when you stand

problems.title: Wrist and forearm strain from typing and the mouse
problems.why: Typing and mouse work hold the wrists bent with small repeated movements for hours. The forearm muscles get tired and tight, and the nerves at the wrist can get irritable.
signs: Ache in the forearm or outside of the elbow
Stiff wrists in the morning or after long typing
Tingling in the fingers that comes and goes

problems.title: Sluggish circulation from not moving
problems.why: Without calf movement, blood pools in the lower legs during long sits. Short movement breaks keep the calf muscle pump working and break up long sitting time.
signs: Heavy or swollen ankles late in the day
Feeling flat or foggy after a long sit
Cold feet at the desk

ergonomics: Screen top at eye level, about an arm's length away
Feet flat on the floor or a footrest
Knees about level with or slightly below the hips
Sit back so the chair supports your low back curve
Elbows close to your sides, about a right angle
Wrists straight and floating, not bent on the desk edge
Mouse close to the keyboard, not out to the side
Laptop on a stand with a separate keyboard
Phone at eye height, or use a headset for calls
Change position at least every 30 to 45 minutes
